parameters.toolDescription: Run an arbitrary GraphQL query or mutation against the Administrate API of your Administrate instance. Use only when no dedicated tool fits. Mutations are namespaced under an entity, for example: mutation ($id: ID!, $input: EventUpdateInput!) { event { update(eventId: $id, input: $input) { errors { label message value } event { id } } } }. Namespaces include event, session, registration, learner, contact, account, courseTemplate, tasks, invoices, opportunities. Every mutation payload exposes errors (label, message, value) plus the mutated object; a non-empty errors list means the write was rejected even though HTTP status is 200. List queries take filters, order, first, offset, after.
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: $fromAI('query', 'The full GraphQL document to execute, as a single string. Use GraphQL variables rather than string interpolation.', 'string'), variables: $fromAI('variables', 'Optional JSON object of GraphQL variables matching the query.', 'json') }) }}

parameters.content:
## Administrate MCP Server
Exposes your Administrate GraphQL API as MCP tools for AI agents and MCP clients.

**Read tools:** search_events, search_course_templates, search_accounts, search_contacts, list_portals.
**Write tools:** create_classroom_event, update_event, add_event_staff, register_contacts_on_event.
**Escape hatch:** graphql_request runs any query or mutation.

**Auth:** the MCP endpoint uses Bearer Auth. Create a Bearer Auth credential with a long random token and select it on the **Administrate MCP Server** trigger before you share the URL.

All tools run as the Administrate OAuth2 credential attached to them, so choose a user with only the permissions you need.

Search tools return the first N results (argument `first`, default 20). To see more, narrow the filters or raise `first`.

parameters.toolDescription: List the WebLink and LMS portals of your Administrate instance. Returns each portal id, url, vanity url, availability state (enabled or disabled), whether it is a booking portal or a self-registration portal, single sign-on flags, and the owning brand. Portals on administratelms.com are LMS (student) portals; portals on administrateweblink.com are WebLink booking or catalogue portals.
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'query mcpPortals($first: Int) { portals(first: $first) { edges { node { id url vanityUrl availabilityState isBookingPortal isSelfRegistrationPortal singleSignOnOnly autoProvisionLearnersViaSingleSignOn brand { id name } } } } }', variables: { first: $fromAI('first', 'Maximum number of portals to return. Default 50.', 'number', 50) } }) }}

parameters.content:
## WARNING: this server can change your data

**The write tools** (create_classroom_event, update_event, add_event_staff, register_contacts_on_event) create and change events, staff assignments and registrations in Administrate.

**graphql_request** runs ANY query or mutation the OAuth2 user is allowed to run. That includes deleting or changing records the dedicated tools never touch.

An AI client connected to this endpoint can use all of these without asking a person first, unless the client itself asks for confirmation.

- Restrict who can reach the MCP endpoint. Keep the Bearer token secret and rotate it if it leaks.
- For read-only use, delete the four write tool nodes **and** graphql_request before activating.
- Test against a non-production instance first.
